name: sqlb
tagline: Typed SQL for Go libraries that own tables and cannot carry an ORM
description: Typed SQL builder for Go: compile-checked columns, joins and scan targets, zero dependencies, Postgres and ClickHouse packages, pgvector and ltree extension sub-packages, and a shared conformance suite that proves a driver executes what the builder renders.

positioning.audience: Authors of Go libraries that ship their own database tables, and the applications that embed them
positioning.wedge: A library that owns tables must let the application join into them without handing over a string and without forcing an ORM on it. sqlb makes the column a typed value, so the library exports it and the compiler checks the application's join.
differentiators: A column is an Expr[T]; comparing, joining or scanning it at the wrong type is a compile error
A query carries its own scan targets, so the column list and the destinations cannot drift
Zero third-party dependencies in the core, enforced by a gate rather than by intent
Only SQL that Postgres, MySQL 8, SQLite and ClickHouse all share lives in the core; engine constructs fail at Build with the construct named
Postgres extensions are sub-packages built on exported guarded constructors, so adding one never edits the engine package
Type safety is verified by a build that must fail, not asserted in prose
A shared conformance suite proves a driver executes what the builder renders
